steps_lead: You leave with a how-to of the steamer pressing the blue shirt, ready to post. The frame already shows that one step.

steps.d: Upload the steamer beside the blue shirt. The press frame is already there, so you are not drawing the lesson.
Use the listing photo or the product link. The spoken line follows the hands and names the press shoppers miss.
Captions can name each press, and you can trim a long pause in the editor before you post the clip.

faq.q: What does a how-to video template include?
faq.a: You get a demo frame for one task, such as pressing a blue shirt with a white steamer. Put your steamer in the frame. An AI avatar can do the press. You do not book a person for this lesson.

faq.q: How does the template become a video?
faq.a: Paste the listing link or drop in the steamer photo, then write the line you want heard. What comes back is a clip of the press you can post. If a pause feels long, shorten it before the file goes up.

faq.q: Why use this instead of hiring someone to film the task?
faq.a: You can change the spoken line after the first press, and the spend stays on the monthly plan rather than a shoot day. A creator's afternoon locks you to one version of the shirt.

faq.q: Who gets the most from a how-to like this?
faq.a: A founder filming in a stock room, and an agency that owes a client a demo of the steamer before the week ends. If the product has a move a buyer must copy, this frame fits.

faq.q: Can I do this if I have never edited a video?
faq.a: Yes. A photo of the steamer on the table is enough to start, even if you have never edited a video.

faq.q: Which products fit a how-to template?
faq.a: The frame fits a product with one move a shopper must copy, like this steamer on a shirt. The spoken line can name that move. The same shape can speak to a different buyer when you swap the photo.

faq.q: Can the how-to use files from my shop?
faq.a: Yes. A logo in the corner and a clip you shot last spring can both go in. The steamer in the photo should be the one you ship, so the demo matches the shelf.

faq.q: Where can I post the finished how-to?
faq.a: Match the frame to the placement. Use 9:16 for a phone story, 1:1 for a square tile, and 16:9 for a wide screen. 4:3 and 3:4 sit in the same picker. YouTube Shorts can take the tall file. A wide screen can take the 16:9 file.

faq.q: Do I pay to use a template?
faq.a: Yes. Templates sit on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A clip spends 24 credits at 6 seconds, 40 at 10, 60 at 15, and 120 at 30. A photo spends 24. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Can I run the how-to in ads and in client work?
faq.a: Yes. A client handoff and a paid placement can use the same steamer clip, and the download has no watermark. Read the license on your plan before you pass the file on.

faq.q: Why not build the ad from a blank file?
faq.a: This frame is already a lesson, so the hour can go to the steamer and the press instead of the shape of the ad. A blank timeline asks you to invent that shape.
